items.text: The Rust desktop app adds the website's menu beside selected words, named and reorderable quick marks with any style or color, grouped lesson contents, a centered Bibles dialog, links to All settings and the privacy policy, and a compact layout for small windows.
Volunteer for Android app testing or join the iOS waiting list through a shared signup link.

screenshot.alt: The mobile testing signup form with Android and iOS choices, empty name and email fields, and email consent.
screenshot.caption: Join Android testing or the iOS waiting list without an account.

items.text: Account settings asks you to sign in again when your session is too old to load devices, and shows progress when retrying sign-in methods and sessions.
The privacy policy link stays at the bottom of Settings on short pages and follows the content on longer pages.
In Come, Follow Me lessons, Explore sits beside the scripture instead of at the far edge of the window.

screenshot.alt: The Come, Follow Me lesson beside an Explore panel for knew, positioned next to the scripture column.
screenshot.caption: Explore stays beside the lesson’s scripture column.

releases.title: Desktop sync, reading and word exploration

items.text: Approve the native desktop app in your browser to connect your account and sync study data.
On desktop, move between chapters with the Left and Right arrow keys, or use the next-chapter link below the verses.

screenshot.alt: The last verse of 1 Nephi 1 with a Next chapter link below it on desktop.
screenshot.caption: Continue reading with the next-chapter link below the verses.

items.text: Scripture and the Journal panel sit together in a centered layout. Log starts with reading only; choose Add a note to expand the full Markdown editor in the same panel.

screenshot.alt: 1 Nephi 1 beside the Journal panel, showing a reading chip, Add a note, a day field and Log reading.
screenshot.caption: Log reading or start a note in the Journal beside the chapter.

items.text: Select a word anywhere in Come, Follow Me to explore study helps, biblical languages, definitions, and word history in a sidebar beside the lesson.

screenshot.alt: The Come, Follow Me lesson Before I Formed Thee in the Belly I Knew Thee beside an Explore sidebar for knew, with a Topical Guide study help.
screenshot.caption: Explore a word selected in the lesson title.

items.text: Adding a Bible on desktop now opens in a centered panel with search and language controls beside the results, plus a language grid for easier browsing.

A privacy policy at versetogether.org/privacy explains what the website and the app keep, what they send to other services, and how to delete your data. It's linked from Settings and the sign-in page.

Delete your account and all the study saved in it from Settings → Account, or at versetogether.org/delete-account. You confirm before anything is deleted, and a deletion that stops partway can be finished later.

releases.title: Your Bibles, feedback and faith tradition

items.text: Manage saved Bibles in Settings → Translations and make any saved translation your default Bible for chapter reading. Your choice is saved on this device; removing the default restores the King James Bible.

screenshot.alt: Bible translations settings showing Your Bibles, the King James Bible marked Default, and the Add Bible button.
screenshot.caption: Manage your Bibles and choose the default in Translations.

items.text: Send suggestions, report problems or request features in Settings → Feedback, with no sign-in required. Leave optional contact details if you would like a reply. If sending fails, your message stays in the form so you can try again.

screenshot.alt: The signed-out Feedback section with an empty feedback message, optional contact field and Send feedback button.
screenshot.caption: Send feedback without signing in, with optional contact details.

items.text: Choose your faith tradition in Settings → Reading. Other denominations keeps Bible reading and your journal while hiding Latter-day Saint scriptures, Come Follow Me, Joseph Smith Translation and study resources. Your choice is saved on this device.

screenshot.alt: Faith tradition settings with Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints selected and an Other denominations option.
screenshot.caption: Choose which faith tradition’s content appears on this device.

releases.title: Unified settings and illustrated release history

items.text: Settings shows one section at a time: your account, reading, study tools or these release notes. Choose one from the pill at the right of the app's header, beside the navigation; on phones and tablets, and in simple mode, the pill sits at the top of the page.

screenshot.alt: The Settings page. The app's navigation is at the top left and, at the top right of the same header, a pill with Account, Reading, Study tools and Release notes, Reading selected. Below, the Reading section spans the page: a John 1:1–3 preview beside text size, typeface, text width and comparison view controls, with simple mode below.
screenshot.caption: Settings' sections in the header, with Reading open.

items.text: Set text size, typeface, text width and comparison view in Settings with a live preview, or reset them. The reader's settings menu has the same controls.

screenshot.alt: The reader's settings menu open over 1 Nephi 1, with simple mode, text size, typeface, text width, comparison view and a link to all settings.
screenshot.caption: The same appearance controls in the reader's settings menu.

items.text: Release notes show each release's version, with screenshots of what changed.

releases.title: Clearer note links and scripture quotes

items.text: In the reader, a note appears once, as a small Note link at the start of each passage it links to. The passage you were reading when you wrote it no longer counts as a link.
Verses quoted together in a note are separated by a blank line.

releases.title: Simpler translations, Explore sections and custom mark colors

items.text: Choosing a Bible translation is simpler, and translations in other languages are easier to find.

screenshot.alt: The Add a Bible screen in the reader: a search field, the language (English) with a Change option, suggested English Bibles each with an Add button, and a link to browse all English Bibles.
screenshot.caption: Adding a Bible from the reader's settings.

items.text: Explore groups study sources into colored, expandable sections and leaves out sections with nothing in them.

screenshot.alt: Explore open for the word “commandments” in 1 Nephi 3:7, with a green Study helps section (Bible Dictionary, Guide to the Scriptures, Topical Guide) and a blue Biblical languages section (Hebrew and Greek), beside the chapter with the word selected.
screenshot.caption: Explore's colored source sections.

items.text: Pick custom colors for highlights and underlines in quick marks, and preview each mark.

screenshot.alt: Quick mark settings: the first preset uses a custom orange color, shown in its preview and its Custom button, above blue and green highlight presets with their color choices.
screenshot.caption: Quick marks with color previews, now in the Study tools tab.

items.text: The Joseph Smith Translation reads more simply inline in the Bible.

releases.title: Joseph Smith Translation, study helps and lesson notes

items.text: Read the Joseph Smith Translation inline in the Bible reader.

screenshot.alt: Mark 9:42–45 in the Bible reader with the Joseph Smith Translation on: a small “JST 9:40–48” label, JST wording read in place with a dotted underline, and JST verse numbers in small type.
screenshot.caption: The Joseph Smith Translation inline in the Bible reader.

items.text: Explore adds scripture study helps and Hebrew and Greek definitions.
Preview scripture links from reader resources without leaving the chapter.
Share focused scripture pages.
Add lesson notes and save excerpts of selected text.
Note backlinks include verse numbers.

releases.title: Lesson artwork to the page edges

items.text: Come, Follow Me lesson artwork reaches the top and edges of the page.

screenshot.alt: The Come, Follow Me lesson for October 19–25, 2026, its painting of a potter's workshop filling the top of the page from edge to edge above the title “Before I Formed Thee in the Belly I Knew Thee”.
screenshot.caption: A lesson's artwork at the top of its page.

items.text: Lesson context stays visible, with a consistent reading width.
The default scripture reading column is narrower.
Come, Follow Me lessons put the scriptures first, with expandable lesson context.

screenshot.alt: A Come, Follow Me lesson reading Jeremiah 1: the line “Read the scriptures. Open the context as you go.”, an opened Chapter context panel, then verses 1–3, then a closed Context for verses 1–3 panel.
screenshot.caption: Scriptures first in a Come, Follow Me lesson.

items.text: Annotate in both Come, Follow Me panes.
Highlights keep the exact text you selected.
Logged reading shows as a line in the margin.
General settings work without signing in.
Mark verses inline with quick marks at the top of the selection menu, and customize the presets.

screenshot.alt: 1 Nephi 3:7 selected in the reader, with the selection menu above it: a row of quick mark highlight and underline buttons at the top, then New Note, Annotate, Resources, Focus scripture and Copy text.
screenshot.caption: Quick marks in the selection menu.

releases.title: Journal and notes without an account

items.text: Save notes and study without signing in.
The journal home page has weekly goals you can edit.

screenshot.alt: The journal home page without an account: a month calendar, weekly goals to study 5 days and write 3 reflections with an Edit goals link, and a reflection prompt for today.
screenshot.caption: The journal home page, without signing in.

items.text: Notes render Markdown, in a more compact note panel.
Verse resources load each Come, Follow Me lesson's complete insights.
The Explore dictionary and etymology panel is more polished.

releases.title: One journal on mobile and desktop

items.text: Journal notes and reading entries work the same on mobile and desktop, with notes beside Log on mobile.
Delete a note, with a confirmation first.
Scripture selection tools are more polished, with direct links to a focused verse.
The Come, Follow Me header has expanding icon controls.
Account settings are simpler.
The October 26 Come, Follow Me guide, pairing scriptures from more than one book.
Sign in directly with Google.
Scripture books have artwork, colored by section.

screenshot.alt: Book of Mormon books in Browse, each card with a painting: green-toned art for the small plates (1 Nephi to Omni) and warm orange art for Mormon's record (Words of Mormon to 4 Nephi).
screenshot.caption: Book artwork in Browse.

items.text: Reading log and notes share one panel in the reader.
A guide's Contents and Log stay in the header at every screen size.

releases.title: Floating navigation, faster browsing and the journal

items.text: Keep journal notes and a reading history, linked from Come, Follow Me.
Navigation is one collapsible floating bar, and Browse cards are illustrated with coordinated artwork.

screenshot.alt: The Browse page under the floating navigation bar and search field, with illustrated cards for this week's Come, Follow Me reading, the journal and each volume of scripture.
screenshot.caption: Floating navigation and illustrated Browse cards.

items.text: Scripture browsing works from local data: chapters open at once and their text fades in.
Search and page controls live in the floating header.
Come, Follow Me opens at this week's lesson, with a cover card for each week.
A new look throughout: a paper grid, ink borders, offset shadows and new typefaces.
Study plans, with reading progress in the reader and a plan builder.
Simple mode hides study tools so only the text remains.
Choose a text width for the reader, and share a passage by link.
Notes moved to a Notebook panel in the reader and a three-column Notes page.
Study each Come, Follow Me lesson beside the scriptures it covers.
Reader navigation is simpler, with chapter progress in the reader's settings.
